findings.title: Fallback locales are never loaded outside controller requests
findings.body: The I18n patch loads locales lazily, and `translate` only loads `config.locale`. The fallback locales (the site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `ensure_loaded!`, which is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Jobs, mailers, rake tasks and console code that call `I18n.t` never load those locales, so lookups that should fall back still return 'translation missing'.

findings.title: Translation cache can store a missing result before fallbacks are loaded
findings.body: The LRU cache key combines the translation key, the locale and the backend object id. If a translation is requested before its fallback locale has been loaded, the 'missing' result is cached. It is then served from the cache even after the fallback locale loads. Changing the `default_locale` setting also leaves stale fallback results in the cache.

findings.title: Fallback lookup does not normalize the locale argument
findings.body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq` does not convert `locale` to a symbol. If it is passed as a string, e.g. 'en', the list contains both 'en' and :en and is not deduplicated. That locale is then loaded and looked up twice, which can also pollute `@loaded_locales`.

findings.title: Fallbacks module is included into whatever backend class is current
findings.body: `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, ...)` depends on which backend is active when the initializer runs. The pluralization line above targets `Simple` explicitly. If a plugin or a later initializer swaps the backend, fallbacks silently stop applying.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
findings.body: The PR adds no specs covering the fallback order (user locale, then site locale, then English) or the loading of fallback locales.
